conventions: Waw standing immediately before a discourse adverb, with one English connective written for the pair: the adverb takes the word and the waw is `unrepresented`, because the word written writes the adverb's own lexeme and leaves the waw's bare coordination unstated. וְגַם → *Moreover* heads on גַּם at JOS.22.7 and וְאַךְ → *Howbeit* on אַךְ at JOS.22.19. Where the ASV writes two words for such a pair, rule 14 divides them as usual and both morphemes are rendered, as the two וְעַתָּה pairs of JOS.22.4 are — *And now* and *therefore now*.

In the recurring חֲצִי שֵׁבֶט / מַטֵּה מְנַשֶּׁה, the phrase's single written *the* follows MACULA's morphology and not the English. Where an article is segmented on מְנַשֶּׁה the article takes it and חֲצִי is bare (JOS.22.7, 9, 10, 11, 21); where no article morpheme stands in the chain the *the* is supplied on חֲצִי (JOS.22.1, 13, 15). The alternation within one chapter is the source's, not a split.
report: One real cross-verse split: a waw standing immediately before a discourse adverb, with one English connective written for the pair, was divided two ways. JOS.22.7 gives 'Moreover' to גַּם and leaves the waw unrepresented; JOS.22.19 gave 'Howbeit' to the waw and left אַךְ unrepresented. Nothing in the source licenses the difference, so JOS.22.19 is patched to match JOS.22.7: אַךְ takes 'Howbeit' and the waw is unrepresented.

Direction chosen by rule 14's closing paragraph, which already supplies the test — the adverb takes the word that writes its own lexeme and the waw takes the connective left over — reinforced by rule 11's priority for the present morpheme whose sense the word carries. 'Howbeit' writes אַךְ's restrictive lexeme as squarely as 'Moreover' writes גַּם's; what the single word leaves unstated is the waw's bare coordination. The corpus's waw-to-'howbeit' units are bare waws with no adverb beside them and do not reach this pair.

BSB disagreements: exactly one is a genuine error — JOS.22.19 אַךְ, ASV unrepresented and BSB represented — and the patch fixes it. The rest are documented convention differences, not corrections: R × 17 and the Rd of קרא לְ at 22.1 and 22.34 (rules 27 and 40), To × several (rule 16), Td × 14 (agreement articles and phrases whose single determiner is a written demonstrative, rules 29, 41, 47), C × 6 (apodosis waws the ASV opens bare, plus בִלְתִּי at 22.25 whose negation is carried inside 'cease'), the repeated נָשִׂיא אֶחָד at 22.14 and the doubled 'from us' at 22.29 (rule 22), and the suffix of חֶצְיוֹ at 22.7, where the ASV writes 'the other half' with no possessive. No accepted edge was changed to improve the aggregate rate.

Candidates read and kept as source-licensed rather than split: בְּתוֹכֵנוּ fused to 'among' at 22.19 but split at 22.31, because the ASV writes one rendering there and a word per morpheme here (rule 30's condition); חֲצִי שֵׁבֶט מְנַשֶּׁה, whose 'the' goes to the article segmented on Manasseh at 22.7/9/10/11/21 and is supplied on חֲצִי at 22.1/13/15, following MACULA's morphology and not the translation; אֲשֶׁר … בָּהּ → 'wherein' fused at 22.9 and 22.33 against אֲשֶׁר … מִמֶּנּוּ → 'from which' split at 22.17, again on rule 30's one-word condition; the בֵּין pairs at 22.25/27/28, counted pair by pair under rule 26; and יָטַב בְּעֵינֵי, one three-morpheme unit headed on the verb at both 22.30 and 22.33.

Also checked end to end for splits the lemma table cannot see, since it is blind to `added` units. The eleven added units are consistent with one another: supplied lexical verbs and their subjects or objects (22.7 'inheritance', 22.12 'of it', 22.23 'it', 22.34 'said they'), supplied connectives and subordinators over clauses with no conjunction morpheme in them (22.18 'seeing', 22.19 'then', 22.24 'and'), the impersonal 'it' of 22.22, the supplied adverbs of 22.24 and 22.28, and the supplied name 'Ed' at 22.34. Each has a written counterpart elsewhere in the chapter that is aligned rather than added — 22.28's כִּי takes 'when' where 22.18 has no conjunction, and 22.30's written object contrasts with 22.12's absent one — so the difference is the Hebrew's each time.

No promotions. The one-word waw-plus-adverb case is already decided by rule 14 as written, so an amendment would restate it; JOS.22.19 was a misapplication rather than a gap. Recorded as a convention instead, together with the Manasseh determiner alternation.
